temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Thin, about ¾ inch (2 cm) 390°F / 200°C · 7 min 400°F / 205°C · 9 min Standard, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) 390°F / 200°C · 9 min 400°F / 205°C · 11 min Thick, about 1½ inches (4 cm) 390°F / 200°C · 12 min 400°F / 205°C · 15 min The white stuff means it is overcooked Salmon has very little margin. It goes from silky to dry in a couple of minutes, and the air fryer is fast enough that those minutes pass quickly. The warning sign is the white curd that appears on the surface: that is albumin, a protein pushed out of the muscle as the fibres tighten. A little is normal; a lot means the fish went past done. Because salmon cooks from the outside in, the only reliable way to time it is by thickness, which is why the table sorts fillets by depth rather than weight. A thin tail piece and a thick centre cut from the same side can need very different times, so cook pieces of similar thickness together, or put the thin pieces in a few minutes later. Worked example Two 1-inch fillets, skin on. Brush the flesh with oil, season, and lay them skin side down. Cook at 390°F for 9 minutes without turning them; a thin ¾-inch fillet needs about 7 minutes and a thick 1½-inch piece about 12. An oven-style air fryer gives 385°F for 9 minutes. A conventional oven takes 400°F for around 11 minutes. How to tell it is done Food safety guidance is 145°F (63°C) in the thickest part, where the flesh turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Many cooks prefer salmon a little less done, at 125–130°F, where the centre is still slightly translucent and very moist; that is a matter of taste for fish bought fresh and handled well. Press gently on the top: done salmon separates along its natural lines. If you see a lot of white albumin, take it out immediately. Before it goes in Let the fillets sit out for ten minutes so the centre is not fridge-cold. Pat them dry and brush the flesh, not the skin, with oil. Skin-on fillets do not need turning: the skin protects the underside and peels off easily afterwards if you do not want it. A piece of perforated parchment stops skinless fillets from sticking to the basket. About 9 minutes at 390°F for a 1-inch fillet. Thin pieces take around 7 minutes and thick centre cuts around 12. Do I flip salmon in the air fryer? No. Cook it skin side down the whole time; turning a delicate fillet tends to break it, and the top colours well in the direct air. What temperature is salmon done at? 145°F (63°C) by food-safety guidance, when it flakes easily. Many people prefer it at 125–130°F, slightly translucent in the middle. Why is there white stuff on my salmon? It is albumin, a protein squeezed out as the fish cooks. A lot of it means the salmon is overcooked; next time take it out a minute or two sooner. What is the oven equivalent for salmon? 400°F for around 11 minutes in a conventional oven, or 400°F for 9 minutes in a fan oven.
